cells.tense: The person has the pen now, and the structure they are building is holding steady.
cells.act: set the finished thing down in a form that keeps
cells.ask: Take one arrangement here that's already fair — what each side gives, what each side gets — and give it a shape that stands when you're not standing there.
cells.core:
There's a structure taking shape, and it's sound. People are giving and getting back in the same motion — the work moves because nobody is carrying a debt they didn't agree to. You can point to the parts. That's what makes it last. And this steady thing doesn't need much from you these days, which is exactly why one careful move is worth making while it's easy.

The move is to give the arrangement a written shape. Pick one that's already fair under this structure — the sharing, the standing plan, whatever runs between you — and put it somewhere it can be read without you there to explain it. The names of what each side gives, what each side gets. Not to lock it. So that on a week when you're absent or tired, the shape stays and people can hold it themselves. It keeps giving while you're elsewhere.
cells.sheetLine: Put the fair thing on paper, so it holds without you.
cells.verb: balancing what is given with what comes back, in the open between people

cells.tense: The person is braced for a fairness that hasn't arrived yet, and the structure is being tightened around it.
cells.act: keep going without checking on anyone else
cells.ask: Carry your own part all week and skip every check on who's giving what.
cells.core:
You can feel the structure getting tighter than it needs to be. Somewhere in it, shares are being tracked — who gave, who owes, what the count is — and the thing meant to hold is starting to creak under the watching. Fairness is real. But here it's been pushed past the point where it keeps anyone safe, and the people in it can feel the tally.

So carry your own part for seven days and keep your eyes on the work. Don't look at anyone else's share. Build what you're building, and don't open the books until it's done. If a gap shows at the end, it shows once, and you can meet it then — not in every hour between. The structure gets to carry weight again.
cells.sheetLine: Counting whose share is whose is making it creak.

cells.tense: The person keeps pouring everything into this structure and it sends nothing back.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Sort your hours into what moved this forward and what didn't.
cells.core:
On this work, you hand over money, hours, care — and it comes back thin. You might not notice it as a lack. You notice that other people's offers land somewhere else, and that when you talk about this you say it's fine. You hand out plenty. What comes back, wherever it went, isn't here at all.

Before asking for anything, look at what you spend. Sort your hours into what moved this work forward and what didn't. Then strike one item off the second sort. That's the whole act. It gives you an hour back, and the hour is for you, spent on anything but this. Something returns from the work in a form you can finally feel.
cells.sheetLine: You give to this and nothing comes back.

cells.tense: The person holds this structure steady while their hands are on it, and doesn't call that theirs.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: When the question of how this runs comes up, let what you know sit unanswered for as long as it takes.
cells.core:
Under this structure there's someone keeping the plain thing working — you know who's overstretched, what the arrangement really is, where it gives. Asked, they'd say it just runs. But someone is behind all that. It's you. And on this question your answer is that you're just being sensible.

So let what you know sit a while. When the question of how this runs comes up, don't rush to name it. Hold both things — that it works, and what you actually see — and say neither yet. The work can go on. You can say it later or not at all. The point is only that you know it's yours before it leaves, so a truth held like this lands where someone else can't take credit for it.
cells.sheetLine: You see how this runs. You call that just being sensible.

cells.place: where the person builds the structure that holds
